key_facts: Elisa de Martel은 Waymo CFO 재직 시 **Waymo를 매출 이전 단계에서 미국 5개 도시 주간 수십만 건 운행 규모로 성장**시켰고 56억 달러 Series C 펀딩을 주도함
이전 Carbon(산업용 3D 프린팅) CFO로 2억6천만 달러 Series D 펀딩 주도, 매출 1억 달러 이상 성장 및 총마진 60%p 이상 개선
Apple에서 10년 이상 제조 재무 등 시니어 재무직 경력, Citroën UK 및 PwC 근무 경력 보유
Wayve는 지난 1년간 **12억 달러(1.2 billion)를 조달**했으며 Uber, Nissan, Stellantis, Qualcomm과 파트너십 체결
Wayve는 런던에서 대중 대상 자율주행 라이드를 시작했고 도쿄 진출을 계획 중
summary_data.why_matters: Waymo의 자본 조달·사업 확장 경험을 가진 CFO 영입은 Wayve가 R&D 단계를 넘어 **대규모 상업 배치를 위한 자본 조달 및 운영 역량 확보**에 나섰음을 시사한다. 이는 AV2.0 진영이 Waymo식 모듈형·고정밀지도 기반 접근과 달리 범용 AI 기반 접근으로 경쟁하려는 자본 경쟁 국면 진입을 의미한다.
summary_data.subject_angle: Wayve는 자동차 OEM(Nissan, Stellantis)과 모빌리티 플랫폼(Uber), 반도체(Qualcomm) 파트너십을 통해 **HD맵·전용 하드웨어 없는 범용 AI Driver를 수백만 대 차량에 확장**하려는 자본 집약적 전략을 취하고 있으며, Waymo 출신 재무 임원 영입은 이 전략의 자금 조달 신뢰도를 높이려는 조치다.
summary_data.focus_angle: 런던에서 대중 자율주행 라이드를 이미 시작했고 도쿄 진출을 계획 중이나 구체적 상용 서비스 규모나 매출은 미확인이며, 이번 CFO 영입은 R&D에서 **자동차·로보택시 양쪽으로의 대규모 상업화 단계로의 전환**을 위한 자본 조달 체제 강화로 해석된다.

cards.body: Wayve has appointed former Waymo CFO Elisa de Martel as Chief Financial Officer as the autonomous driving technology company moves into a larger commercialization phase across automotive and robotaxi markets. De Martel brings more than two decades of financial leadership experience across technology and automotive companies and will oversee Wayve’s global finance organization from Sunnyvale, California. She most recently served as CFO of Waymo, where she led financial strategy and capital planning while the autonomous driving company expanded from a pre-revenue operation to hundreds of thousands of weekly trips across five U.S. cities. De Martel also led Waymo’s $5.6 billion Series C financing. Before Waymo, she served as CFO of industrial 3D printing company Carbon, where she led a $260 million Series D financing, helped grow revenue beyond $100 million and improved gross margin by more than 60%. Earlier in her career, de Martel spent more than a decade in senior finance positions at Apple, including manufacturing finance, and also held roles at Citroën UK and PricewaterhouseCoopers. The appointment comes as Wayve accelerates commercialization of its Wayve AI Driver. Wayve describes the platform as a single end-to-end AI system designed to operate across different vehicles, markets and product categories without relying on high-definition maps, extensive hand-coded rules or custom hardware. That model is central to what Wayve calls AV2.0, its approach to building autonomous driving systems through generalized AI rather than developing separate highly customized stacks for individual cities or vehicles. De Martel’s experience financing and scaling Waymo gives Wayve an executive familiar with the capital requirements and operating challenges involved in moving autonomous driving technology from R&D toward widespread commercial deployment. Wayve has raised $1.2 billion over the past year and formed partnerships with companies including Uber, Nissan, Stellantis and Qualcomm. The company has also launched public autonomous rides in London and plans to bring rides to Tokyo. Max Warburton, who has served as Wayve’s CFO since 2024, will transition into a strategic advisory role supporting the leadership team. Wayve ultimately plans to deploy its AI Driver across millions of vehicles spanning both consumer automotive and mobility applications. KEY QUOTES: “AV2.0 is an innovative, capital-efficient approach to autonomy, and I’m looking forward to scaling the AI Driver globally with our team and partners.” Elisa de Martel, Incoming Chief Financial Officer of Wayve “I couldn’t be more excited about the experience and passion Elisa brings in autonomy and deep tech, and I look forward to partnering with her to scale the company as we launch the Wayve AI Driver in millions of vehicles across the automotive and mobility industry.” Alex Kendall, Co-Founder and CEO of Wayve
